column1: # EnglishSyllables fixture: 1,000 English words and their syllable counts, derived from CMUdict.
# Format: word<TAB>syllables. Lines starting with # are comments.
# A word's syllable count is the number of phones with a stress digit (0, 1 or 2) in its CMUdict entry.
# THE SAMPLING RULE (fixed before any heuristic was measured against it):
#   1. Lowercase every CMUdict headword; count each pronunciation's stress digits.
#   2. Keep headwords made only of a-z (drops apostrophes, digits, dots, parentheses, hyphens).
#   3. Keep a headword only if all its pronunciations give the same count (1,672 ambiguous words dropped).
#   4. Keep only English dictionary words: the headword is a web2 line made only of a-z (web2 capitalises
#      names and acronyms), OR it is a regular inflection of one: +s, +es, y->ies, +ed, e+d, doubled
#      consonant+ed, y->ied, +ing, e-drop+ing, doubled consonant+ing, +er, +est, e+r, e+st, doubled
#      consonant+er/+est, y->ier, y->iest, +ly, y->ily. (web2 lists headwords only: walked, loves, dreams
#      and eyes are all absent from it, so without the inflections no -ed or -s form would be tested.)
#   5. Order the 49,348 survivors (31,291 dictionary words, 18,057 inflections) by the SHA-256 hex digest
#      of the word's UTF-8 bytes, ascending. THIS FILE IS THE FIRST 1,000.
#   The heuristic was tuned only on words after the first 1,000 (never on this file).
